relevance_note: The paper describes individual SSADH deficiency patients with ALDH5A1 genotypes, e.g. 'The genotype was compound heterozygous c.1294A>C (p.Met432Leu); c.610-2A>G.'
method_note: Natural-history study progress report (28 recruited patients). Most data are group-level (Table 2 counts by age cohort, EEG and neuropsychology counts); no per-patient table, so Table 2 counts and percentages assign nothing to anyone. Six in-scope people got rows: unnamed person 1 = the lowest-functioning / maximum-severity patient (first mentioned in the Abstract); unnamed person 2 = the highest-functioning patient with normal IQ; unnamed person 3 = the single subject with generalized spike-and-wave on EEG, which the text ties to Figure 5 (the 8-year-old in the Figure 5 legend; I treated text and legend as the same person); unnamed persons 4 and 5 = the two subjects with focal spikes, 'ages 5 and 9', assigned in printed order (the two are distinguishable only by age); ref Yamakawa et al 2012 patient = the previously published 23-month-old boy with the same c.1294A>C variant (Discussion). The paper does not say whether unnamed person 3 (Figure 5) is the same person as unnamed person 1 (who had hypsarrhythmia and seizures); they were kept separate (never merge). Persons 2, 4 and 5 cannot be the Figure 5 patient or each other by the stated EEG/seizure findings. The 'sharp waves in two' subjects were not given rows (count only, no individual detail). Ages of persons 3-5 are ages at the EEG, recorded as age at last evaluation; the ages '5' and '9' print no unit, so no ISO value was given. Person 1's Clinical Severity Score of 5/25 (the scale minimum) implies the lowest level in every subdomain, but this was not used to fill any feature (inference). Person 2's severity score 20/25 and 'highest functioning ... Movement Assessment Battery' were not converted to features. Person 2's normal IQ (87) is recorded as intellectual disability excluded (D-27). Person 2's two variants are not called compound heterozygous (or anything else), so zygosity is not reported for person 2; c.610-2A>G and c.612G>A have no stated variant class. 'novel' and 'known variant present in over 5% of the patients' were not treated as pathogenicity classifications. Disease label and diagnosis basis for the study participants come from the recruitment statement and the eligibility criterion (confirmed via 4-OH-butyric aciduria and pathological ALDH5A1 variants); the gene symbol is not printed next to the individual variants, so its span is the eligibility text. is_proband and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (not stated). The JSON was assembled with a short Python script from my own reading; no table was transcribed by script. No internal contradictions found.
